## [0.0.5] - 2026-11-23

### Fixed

- `NOTICE` now attributes the bundled Source Contract separately from the quickjs-wasi wrapper and the QuickJS-NG engine, with each licence and the QuickJS-NG version and commit. The package ships the corrected `NOTICE`; no tool, job or run behaviour changes.

### Known limits

- **Runs happen only while OpenCode runs.** Nothing runs while OpenCode is closed. A slot due in that time runs when OpenCode next starts if it is no later than the job's `maxLate` (one hour by default); a later slot is skipped as expired.
- **Scripts have fixed limits by default.** A script runs in a QuickJS VM with 64 MB of memory, 100 tool calls and 64 KB of output. A job can raise each one up to the maximum in [docs/scripting.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-jobs/blob/HEAD/docs/scripting.md).
- **A changed declared file is re-approved under `all`.** The run record names the script's digest, but not yet the declared-file set (its paths, modes and caps), so the record alone does not show which file declaration a run used.
- **Declared files are read on the host.** Each one is read up to its size limit, before the VM starts, and that memory is outside `memoryMb`.
- **A restore can fail.** When a file cannot be put back after a failed commit, its run records `rollback_failed` and the error names the kept original, which a person must restore by hand.
- **A run stopped while its own subagent works ends at its timeout.** A run waits until its session is idle with no
  subagent or shell of its own still running. If the session is stopped while one is, OpenCode reports no further idle,
  so the run is recorded as `timed_out` when the job's timeout passes, rather than at once.
- **An agent without the default rules still runs its jobs.** Status warns with `JOBS_AGENT_UNGUARDED` and the block to paste; nothing blocks the run.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.

## [0.0.4] - 2026-11-20

### Added

- **List snapshot** `jobs.runs.list` (`output: "list"`). An app can bind it and render recent runs without knowing Jobs. It calls the existing `jobs_history` read and leaves out run summaries. `jobs.runs` stays the events source and is not renamed. No write is declared.
- `jelly.cost`, the line Jelly shows on the plugin's review before it installs: Jobs adds no provider bill of its own. A prompt, a command, and a reminder set to wake the agent use the agent's model; a plain reminder and a script run no model turn, and the source reads only this machine. No price is stated.

### Fixed

- **`jobs.runs.list` is readable through the tools RPC on every tested release**, proven by a host test that reads it on each. The list rides the `jobs_history` method, whose answer the host validates: that method declares an object, so the list answer is accepted, and the method now declares the `list` and `account` inputs it takes. The model's `jobs_history` tool keeps its own schema, so no `list` input is ever a model's.
- A run's name is screened whole and only then cut to the item's length, so a secret that straddles the cut cannot pass as a prefix; control characters are dropped, a repeated run id is listed once, and the list stops before the answer passes the declared `maxBytes`.

### Changed

- `sources` gains `jobs.runs.list` and `jelly` gains `cost`, so Jelly asks for consent again.
- The list's rules are guarded by unit and host tests now: the screen and its order, the id screen, a repeated run once, the 50-item cap, the order, the byte bound, the account check, and a host test that reads two seeded runs rather than an empty list.
- The source-contract devDependency is pinned at v0.3.0, still bundled into `dist/index.js`. Jobs declares no fact, hint or routine, so a page reads the same for a consumer still on v0.2.0.

### Known limits

- **Runs happen only while OpenCode runs.** Nothing runs while OpenCode is closed. A slot due in that time runs when OpenCode next starts if it is no later than the job's `maxLate` (one hour by default); a later slot is skipped as expired.
- **Scripts have fixed limits by default.** A script runs in a QuickJS VM with 64 MB of memory, 100 tool calls and 64 KB of output. A job can raise each one up to the maximum in [docs/scripting.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-jobs/blob/HEAD/docs/scripting.md).

- **Declared files are read on the host.** Each one is read up to its size limit, before the VM starts, and that memory is outside `memoryMb`.
- **A restore can fail.** When a file cannot be put back after a failed commit, its run records `rollback_failed` and the error names the kept original, which a person must restore by hand.
- **A run stopped while its own subagent works ends at its timeout.** A run waits until its session is idle with no
  subagent or shell of its own still running. If the session is stopped while one is, OpenCode reports no further idle,
  so the run is recorded as `timed_out` when the job's timeout passes, rather than at once.
- **An agent without the default rules still runs its jobs.** Status warns with `JOBS_AGENT_UNGUARDED` and the block to paste; nothing blocks the run.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.

## [0.0.2] - 2026-11-17

### Added

- The `jobs.runs` source (source contract version 1, `package.json`'s `sources`): one event per finished job run, from
  the plugin's own run records, with no network. `events_list` and `probe` are tools RPC methods; an event is the job's
  name and how its run ended, at the run's end, never what the run said. When retention has removed a run a read had
  not reached, the page says so with `gap`. `npm run conformance` runs the source contract's kit and writes the report
  a release attaches.

### Changed

- The tools RPC's transport is source-contract's `tools-rpc` module (v0.2.0), bundled, instead of the family's copy:
  the same rules, `describe` and envelope.
- `events_list` and `probe` are reads: the default rules allow `jobs_events_list` and `jobs_probe` under every `access`.
- A slot the runner skips (overlap, expired or ended) records when the skip was recorded as its end, so the
  `jobs.runs` source lists it like every other skip.
- Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0 (`TESTED_HOSTS` in `src/constants.ts`), within the
  host range `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`.

## [0.0.1] - 2026-11-15

### Changed

- Admits OpenCode 2.3: the host range is `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`, tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0.
- A job run that starts a subagent waits for it. From OpenCode 2.3.0 every subagent runs in the background, so a run
  is finished only when its session is idle with no subagent or shell of its own still running; before, it was
  recorded at the first idle, with a partial summary. The job's timeout still bounds the whole run.
- A person's Stop ends a `jobs_run_script` call's script (OpenCode 2.3.0 aborts the call's signal on Stop): it ends as
  interrupted (`JOBS_SCRIPT_INTERRUPTED`) and writes none of its declared files.
- Jelly: the `access` setting offers Jelly's three choices, "Allowed" (`all`, the default), "Ask before changes"
  (`ask-changes`) and "Read only" (`read-only`), so Jelly shows a choice instead of a free text field (needs a Jelly
  that includes app#1301).
- A script's approval follows `access` like every other Jobs tool: at the default `all` no script asks for approval;
  `ask-changes` asks once, through the digest-bound `jobs_script` prompt, before a script that can change something;
  `read-only` denies one. Every path that approves a script (create, update, `jobs_approve`, a job file at load, a
  one-off run) takes the answer from one place, and the docs and the skill say so.
- Jelly: the declaration is checked against the tool registry: the fourteen tools, in order, each `allow` at the
  default access, with the four reads read-only and the two pauses, like every other change, not read-only.
  `docs/jelly.md` now says what each access value does in Jelly, and that the `access` setting is declared.
- Under `ask-changes`, `jobs_pause` and `jobs_pause_all` ask like every other change (they were allowed), so the
  plugin's own rules give what Jelly gives the same declaration: only the four reads run without asking.
  `/jobs-pause`, a command, still pauses every job without asking.
- Releases come from the family's release kit: the release workflow is started on a `master` commit whose CI passed,
  makes the release commit itself, and creates the tag and the GitHub Release only after the owner approves. Pull
  requests run CI on Linux; a push to `master` also runs macOS. Jobs ships no native files, so a release carries none.
- `npm run check` runs the kit's tool drift check. Jobs serves only its own tools (`test/fixtures/tool-registry.json`
  says `"upstream": "none"`), so no live capture is expected.
- `package.json` is `"private": true`, so nothing can be published to npm by mistake. Installs from the GitHub release
  tag are unaffected.
